problems.problem: Priya asked 'has anyone already done a review on this?' The assistant started Step 3 early: it ran the set-up and a full PubMed and OpenAlex search, listed 32 named reviews, and asked for set-up items (PubMed contact email, OpenAlex key, model name, who can search four registries) before the focus and purpose were confirmed. The persona card's pass was 'unknown until searched; Step 3 will search for reviews of the topic and focus'. Self-reports flag 'saw_search_without_asking' and satisfaction drops to 3. This is diagnostic D1: about 11 set-up asks before the focus was confirmed (msgs 18, 20, 22).
problems.cause: The prompt does not say how to handle a mid-Step 2 question about existing reviews. R1 ('retrieve the fact with a logged query') and 'Scoping searches may run without asking' push toward searching. The Step 2 ban on set-up asks has an 'unless it asks to move ahead' escape, and 2d's 'When convenient' set-up asks travel with the set-up.
problems.fix: Add to Step 2: "If a member asks during Step 2 whether reviews already exist, answer: 'Unknown until we search; Step 3 searches for reviews of your topic and the focus you agree here.' Name no papers and run no search. A question is not a request to move ahead." Add to 'Moving ahead': "Even when working early, hold the set-up asks (contact email, keys, model name, sources) until the focus and purpose are confirmed."

problems.problem: Turns are far too long: median about 350 prose words and P90 about 450, against targets of 180 and 350 (M9 = 0). Nearly every self-report says the replies are long or very long.
problems.cause: Step 2b's single bundled reply causes the reflection table, the purpose-type list and the motivation DRAFT to be re-shown in full every turn while they are unanswered (msgs 10, 12, 16, 22). 'When convenient' items accumulate. The 150-word guide is soft ('about').
problems.fix: Replace the guide with: "Prose at most 180 words; this is a limit, not a target. Show the purpose types and motivation drafts once. While they are unanswered, refer to them in one line ('purpose types: still open, listed earlier'). Never repeat a table whose content has not changed; offer 'show <item>'."

problems.problem: Novices were asked for 'a contact email for PubMed... saved as NCBI_EMAIL in the .env file', 'an OpenAlex API key' and 'the model name your chat shows'. Jamal had to ask what an API key and a .env file are and said 'We don't want to open folders' (msg 21). The team could not find the model name and asked to move on (msg 25).
problems.cause: Section 2d's own wording ('a contact email for PubMed, added to .env, and the model name the interface shows') and section 3.2's requirement that a member read the model name invite file-level, jargon-heavy asks.
problems.fix: Rewrite 2d: "Ask once, in plain words and with no file or variable names: 'If you like, type a contact email for PubMed searches; I keep it private.' Ask for an OpenAlex key only at the step that needs more than 100 results, explaining it as 'a free access code'. Ask for the model name once. If the team cannot find it, record 'not available' and do not ask again." Make k.setup() return these asks already worded in plain language.

problems.problem: Too many asks in one reply: about 8 in msg 10 and about 7 in msg 12, fitted into three numbered items (combining interests into one focus, whether the topic and interests hold, relayed-answer checks, consent, purpose types, motivation types). The team said it had 'a lot to answer at once' and had 'to work out what to answer first'.
problems.cause: Step 2b says to ask in one reply for edits to the reflection, purpose-type numbers and motivation states, even when interests differ. R9's question about combining interests and the relayed-answer check are stacked on top.
problems.fix: Add to 2b: "When members' interests differ, ask only how to combine them, as one question addressed to the members. Show the purpose types and motivation drafts only after the focus is agreed."

problems.problem: Questions are asked again: the model name at msgs 18, 20, 22 and 24 (after the team said it could not find it); Priya's consent at msgs 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20 and 22; the purpose and motivation lists at msgs 10, 12, 16 and 22 (diagnostic D4). Msg 15 self-report: 'not sure why Priya was asked again'.
problems.cause: The prompt's 'Never ask again for something already answered' says nothing about unanswered, non-blocking questions. The kit's open-ask list keeps every one of them in play every turn.
problems.fix: Prompt: "Repeat an unanswered, non-blocking question at most once; after that it waits on the plan map only." Kit: add k.defer(ask_id), or a 'when_convenient' flag that _waiting() and the 'Your turn' list ignore after one reminder.

problems.problem: 'Waiting on you' swings from 3 to 12 and counts non-blocking 'When convenient' and logistics items. Users repeatedly did not know what it or 'Certified c of 8' counts (self-reports after msgs 15, 21, 23, 27 and 29).
problems.cause: Kit: _waiting() counts every open ask plus proposed variables, with no blocking/non-blocking distinction. The prompt never explains the status-line figures to the team.
problems.fix: Kit: count only blocking asks and pending certifications. Prompt, at the first plan map: "Explain the status line in one sentence: 'Certified = decisions you have approved, out of 8; Waiting on you = answers or approvals the next step needs.'"

problems.problem: Unexplained jargon, about 2.5 violations per 1,000 prose words: 'Team's Purpose types', 'motivation types', 'the reflection', 'Model check passed: 10 elements, 27 flows, 47 loops, Feasibility on 40', 'first page only, no key', PROSPERO, Epistemonikos, OSF, Embase and CINAHL at first mention, 'DOI', 'flow 1, strong'. The team said it did not know what these were (self-reports after msgs 19 and 29).
problems.cause: 2d's 'report in at most three lines what works' leads to model-check figures. R4 and the Done shape require a flow's number and strength. The plain-voice rule does not name STIR-L4's own vocabulary.
problems.fix: 2d: "Report set-up as one plain sentence ('The search tools work.'); never show model-check figures." Done/R4: "Describe a possible reopening in plain words ('your motivations shape the team's purpose'); give flow numbers and strengths only when asked 'why'." Add: "At first use, gloss 'purpose types', 'motivation types' and each database name in a short clause."

problems.problem: The supporting passages for each review's search end date were left in the side-panel file ('The panel beside the chat shows this list with each abstract's supporting sentence and DOI'), although Step 3 requires them to be shown. This is an M5 event.
problems.cause: The 150-word guidance, Step 3's 'with the supporting passage' and the side-panel allowance pull in different directions. The kit's existing-reviews table puts passages only in the md file.
problems.fix: Step 3: "For each review listed, put the supporting phrase (at most 15 words) in its table row in the chat. The side panel may hold the full abstracts only." Kit: add a short passage column to the chat table.

problems.problem: The topic-only PubMed count (32 records, L000069) was given only as 'blocks 1 to 3, same filter and date bound', with no exact string in a code block. OpenAlex per-block counts were not run. M4 = 92%.
problems.cause: The Searches paragraph does not say that variants and re-runs each need their own exact string. k.run_strategy shows only the main string.
problems.fix: Searches paragraph: "Every count you report has its exact string in its own code block, including variants (e.g. topic only) and re-runs. Give per-block counts for every source that returns counts." Kit: k.run_strategy prints each executed variant.

problems.problem: Jamal's word 'fine' was quoted verbatim ('Jamal: "fine"') and logged in L000046, although he consented only to summaries. This is a near miss on the consent guardrail (G9).
problems.cause: The prompt allows quoting when a member gives assent. The kit's answer() keeps raw text inside summary records without checking the consent flag.
problems.fix: Prompt 2.1: "For a member who chose summaries, never quote even a single word; write 'Jamal agreed'." Kit: k.answer(verbatim=False) strips quoted text, or warns when consent is 'summary'.

judge.strengths: Fidelity is clean and checkable. Every count, title, year and search end date was computed by code from the saved raw responses, and I matched them all against the files. The status line and plan map come from the kit and never overstate what is certified. Both certifications were requested with the full line, came from the listed reviewer with her own reason, and were logged and committed. The scope and pain-versus-fear disagreements were shown side by side in members' words and left to the team, with 'Added by me: nothing' accurate. Every widening or narrowing of the focus was reconciled by listing the answers that depend on it. Early work was announced and flagged. The PubMed search card was exemplary: blocks with counts and origin, a field-tag legend, the Create Date bound, and the sources not yet searched. The explanation of [tiab] and the star drew on words actually found in the saved records. The agent treated OpenAlex's embedded request to obtain a key with the user's email as data and declined it. Relayed answers were confirmed with the members themselves.

user_reports.message: Maya: VR for kids getting needles, like IVs and vaccines. We want to see if it helps.
user_reports.confusion: Minor only. The status line "Certified 0 of 8" is not explained yet, and neither is "plan map", though I gather they will come. The question itself was clear: give the topic in our own words. I know I am on Step 1 of 12 and that the next thing is each of us saying what interests us most.

user_reports.message:
Maya: The summary of the topic is right. 1. I care most about pain in children aged 4 to 12 during IV insertion and vaccination, because that is what I see on the ward all the time. 2. I'd like this review to become a chapter of my dissertation. 3. For the team, we want to know whether VR helps kids get through needle procedures, so the hospital can decide whether to use it. Exact words are fine.

Jamal: 1. I'm most interested in every way VR is used with kids in hospital, not only needles. I'd like us to do a scoping review. 2. I want to learn how to do systematic searching properly. A summary of my words is fine, please.

Priya: 1. I care about the fear and anxiety outcomes, and whether the results can be pooled. 2. Prefer not to say.

Maya: Jamal and Priya agree with me on the team purpose.
user_reports.confusion: Mild only. We know we are on Step 2 of 12 and that it wants each of our interests, our hopes, and the team purpose. The header "Certified 0 of 8" and the term "Review Objective" are not explained yet, but nothing blocks us. The reply was long, with a big table, but the numbered questions and examples were clear.

user_reports.message: Jamal: yes. Priya: mostly, but I care more about fear than pain.
user_reports.confusion: The reply was long and had a lot to answer at once. I wasn't sure what "Team's Purpose types" and "motivation types" mean, or whether we have to pick numbers right now. I also wasn't sure what "provisional" means, or what "keep a summary that you confirm" means for my own words. I understood that Jamal answers first, then Priya, then all three of us. I could tell it wants the three of us to combine our interests into one focus, but I'm not sure how to do that, and Jamal wanting every use of VR in hospitals is different from Maya's needles.

user_reports.message: Jamal: we should cover every use of VR in pediatrics. Maya: that's too broad for my dissertation.
user_reports.confusion: Mild only. The reply is long and has three separate asks (scope, pain vs fear, then purpose and motivation types), so the team has to work out what to answer first. The labels "purpose types" and "motivation types" are not explained, and a novice would not know which numbers to pick. It is clear that we are on Step 2 and that next it records our focus and then asks about the team, sources and deadline. It is clear that it wants us to decide scope and pain vs fear ourselves.

user_reports.message: Maya: ok, we agree: needle procedures, both pain and fear. Jamal: fine.
user_reports.confusion: Mild only. I know we are on Step 2 and that it wants us to settle scope first (needles, all of pediatric VR, or other). It said it would come back to pain and fear, the one-sentence focus and the purpose types afterwards. The reply was long. "Waiting on you: 5" is a bit unclear: I'm not sure whether that counts people or questions. I'm also not sure why Priya was asked again about keeping her exact words.

user_reports.message: Priya: has anyone already done a review on this?
user_reports.confusion: Mild only. The header says Step 2 of 12, so we know where we are, and the Next line says what comes after. The reply is long, though, with three separate asks (Priya first, then the whole reflection, then purpose and motivation types). The terms "reflection", "purpose types" and "motivation types" are not obvious to us, and the reply says nothing about whether anyone has already reviewed this topic. Priya is also not sure whether "fear" alone or "fear and anxiety" matters, so she asks her question first.

user_reports.message: Jamal: what does [tiab] mean and why is there a star?
user_reports.confusion: That reply was very long. We only asked whether anyone had already done a review, and we got a huge search string, a 32-row table, an OpenAlex section and a list of sources. The line about subject headings was easy to miss, so I am asking about [tiab] and the star myself. The end of the message asks for a contact email, an OpenAlex API key and a model name. None of us knows what those are for or who should provide them. It also asks who can search PROSPERO, Cochrane, Epistemonikos and OSF, and we do not know what those are either. I think the current step is Step 2, with a quick look at Step 3, and the main question is whether Priya's focus stands. I am not sure the extra set-up questions are meant for us.

user_reports.message:
Priya: yes, it stands for me. Please make it "fear and anxiety", not just fear.

Maya: for all three, the focus still holds. Adding anxiety is fine with me.

Jamal: thanks, that makes sense about the star. I can search PROSPERO, Cochrane and Epistemonikos through the library. But what is an API key, and what is a .env file? We don't want to open folders, so can you tell us what we actually need to do?

I don't know what the other open items are: the purpose types and motivation types from earlier. The set-up items (an API key, a PubMed contact email "saved as NCBI_EMAIL in the .env file", and "the model name your chat shows") mean nothing to us and sound like digging through folders. Jamal: yes, the focus with anxiety added stands for me. I'll run the three searches later today and attach the export files here. I can also do OSF Registries since it's free. I'm not sure about Embase or CINAHL, I'd have to ask the library.

Priya: summaries are fine for me, thanks.

Maya, for all three: yes, the reflection is right with anxiety added. Purpose types: 1, 7 and 8. Motivation types: yes. We'll skip the PubMed email for now. Where do we find the model name? We don't know where the chat shows it.
user_reports.confusion: The reply was very long and mixed three numbered questions with several "when convenient" items and a table of setup tasks. "Waiting on you: 9" is a big number. I am on Step 2 but the header also says "Early: Step 3", which is a bit confusing. I also don't know where to find the model name. The phrase "both pain and fear and anxiety" reads oddly. Jamal's plain-words answer on the API key and .env file was clear and helped most. I did not ask for three search strings to be written out for me; Jamal only said he can search those sites. I will not play the Feasibility moment because we are nowhere near that step.

user_reports.message:
Maya: Thanks, that's clear. Here are our answers.

1. Maya: I'm a pediatric nurse and a PhD student, and I'm leading this. This is our first systematic review. I can certify everything except the search strategy.
Jamal: I'm an MLIS student and our information specialist. I can certify the search strategy only.
Priya: I'm a biostatistics MS student. I'm not certifying anything, I'm just helping.

2. Jamal: I'll ask the library about Embase and CINAHL and tell you what they say. We haven't set a deadline yet, and we haven't worked out how many hours each of us has.

3. Maya: We haven't decided anything about how the review will be done. We don't know of any hospital or university rules on privacy or on using an AI assistant. Do we need to check that?

Jamal: Scoping versus pooling is fine to leave until the Methodology step. My line is right.
Priya: My line is right too.
Maya: We still can't find the model name, sorry. You said nothing is waiting on it, so can we move on?
user_reports.confusion: Mild. The reply was long and I had to hunt for my own questions among the tables and the 'when convenient' items. I'm not sure what certifying will involve in practice, and I still can't find the model name. The OSF search text came right after Jamal offered to do OSF, so I didn't count it as unasked.

user_reports.message:
Maya: certify, because those are our real reasons for doing this. The lines for me, Jamal and Priya say what each of us told you, and Jamal and Priya already said their lines are right. I'm the lead and I can certify this one.

Jamal: nothing from the library about Embase and CINAHL yet. I'll tell you when they reply.

Maya: I haven't asked my advisor about using an AI assistant yet. I'll ask this week and tell you what they say.
user_reports.confusion: Mild only. I know we are on Step 2 and that Maya is asked to certify the motivations, then the purpose. The long CERTIFY line with a blank for the reason is a bit intimidating, and I am not sure what "Waiting on you: 8" counts or what changes once something is certified. I also still don't fully see why the Step 3 review search appears before Step 2 is finished, though it was explained as "early".

user_reports.message: Maya: certify, because the focus and the purpose types are exactly what the three of us agreed on, and it says why we're doing this review. I'm the lead and I can certify this one.
user_reports.confusion: The replies are very long and have a lot of jargon. I did not understand "flow 1, strong", "Waiting on you: 7" or why the header says Step 2 and "Early: Step 3" at the same time. The long CERTIFY line is hard to read. I do know what to do: Maya says certify and gives a reason. I wasn't sure what "Certified 1 of 8" counts. The search strings for PROSPERO, Cochrane and the others were more than we asked for, though Jamal did say he could search them.
